# SPD-064 — Edit and Bash hooks: a member may write any path outside every registered project (~/.gitconfig, ~/.claude/settings.json, shell rc files, ~/.ssh) because the path rule stops at project boundaries

## Brief
edit_reason in bin/spud_ledger.py (about line 6221) resolves the target against the registered projects and, when it lies inside none of them, returns no reason: `inside = project_paths(ctx, con, path, cwd); if not inside: return None, None`. So the path rule that holds a member to its deliverable globs stops at project boundaries, and a bound member may Write, Edit or redirect into any file outside every project: `~/.gitconfig` (which SPD-047 shows git reads with nothing on the line, aliases and program-naming keys included), `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.claude/agents/` (user-level hooks, permissions and the spudagent definition that `project sync --all` writes there), `~/.zshrc` and the other shell rc files, `~/.ssh/config`, LaunchAgents, and anything else in Eric's home. Law 2 and Law 5 say a member writes only its deliverables; the edit hook was meant to refuse it every other path. The gap is presumably deliberate for the session scratchpad under /private/tmp/claude-501/ and the system temp directories, where members run probes and differential harnesses (Cherie did for SPD-047), so the design question is where the line goes: allow only the scratchpad and temp roots and refuse everything else outside a project (fail closed, the rule's shape everywhere else), or a denylist of sensitive homes. Spud leans to the allowlist. Whatever the line, the Bash hook's redirection check and the edit hook must draw it the same way, and Spud's own session keeps writing its own files and the memory directory under ~/.claude/projects/.

Evidence: proposal 66 (SPUD-047/Cherie): "a path outside every registered project is refused to nobody, so a member's Write to ~/.gitconfig is allowed"; bin/spud_ledger.py lines 6221-6223 read by Spud at SPD-047's return. Found while closing SPD-047; out of its brief, which is git's reading of config files, and wider than the git half proposal 66 keeps.

## Size, persona and model decision
Eric's batch of 2026-09-15: thirteen hook tickets on one worktree and branch (spd-064-hook-batch), five engineers on opus in series, since every one edits bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py and parallel members need disjoint deliverables. Cluster A, first: SPD-064 with SPD-063, one engineer, no children. Spud's design decision: the allowlist. A caller with an agent_id in a Spud session may write outside every registered project only under the session scratchpad root (/private/tmp/claude-<uid>/) and the system temp roots; everything else outside a project is refused, fail closed, with the Edit hook and the Bash redirection check drawing the same line. Spud's own session, plain sessions and Eric's memory directory under ~/.claude/projects/ are unchanged.
